newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - AWB Report - Rain damages Australian crop.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - AWB Report - Rain damages Australian crop.

text.p: The 75 mm of rain which fell across the harvest in Central Queensland in three days last week did considerable damage to the wheat crop, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said in its weekly grain market report.
"Much of the crop has been reduced to feed grade and the extent of the damage wont't be fully assessed until harvest is under way again," AWB said.
The rain damage follows an increase in the AWB's wheat crop estimate to 20 million tonnes after increased estimated yields in all Australian states.
The damage comes on top of problems with the Canadian crop resulting in as much as six million tonnes being downgraded to feed quality, AWB said.
The AWB indicator price was unchanged at A$150.74 a tonne during the past week.

While feed barley prices came under pressure in Queesland and New South Wales dropping by as much as A$6 a tonne in the past week, the feed grain complex of barley, red wheat and triticale remained firm in Victoria, AWB said.
Canola dropped below the A$400 a tonne mark this week but good international demand for vegetable protein meal continues to support pulse prices.
Twenty two thousand tonnes of Australian wheat landed in Kenya this week.
Argentine wheat was offered at A$179 and French wheat at A$216 for Nov Dec and A$211 for January and February.
